source.quote: The Create EventSub Subscription API endpoint has been updated to provide the id of the existing EventSub subscription when a 409 Conflict is returned.

tasks.reasoning: The repo creates and lists EventSub webhook subscriptions directly over HTTP, so this change touches both call sites. It is additive: nothing breaks. The create call never checks for 409, though, so the migration agent should handle a 409 by reading the returned existing subscription id instead of treating the body as a fresh creation. That may also remove the need for the separate GET lookup when re-subscribing. No change is required for the conduit_id parameter on GET.

callSites.why: Calls POST /helix/eventsub/subscriptions and returns response.json() without checking the status code. A 409 Conflict body now carries the id of the existing subscription, so callers get a different payload shape on duplicates.
Calls GET /helix/eventsub/subscriptions to map type->id, which is the lookup the new 409 id makes unnecessary. The new conduit_id filter is additive and needs no change here.

## Create EventSub Subscription 409 Conflict now returns existing subscription id; Get EventSub Subscriptions accepts conduit_id [Verified]

### Change

create_subscription in src/app.py now detects HTTP 409 and surfaces the existing subscription id (as result["existing_id"], also printed), extracted defensively by a new extract_existing_id helper. Added tests/test_conflict.py. The conduit_id GET parameter needs no change.

Files touched:
- `src/app.py`
- `tests/test_conflict.py`

### Why

Changelog 2026-04-17: "The Create EventSub Subscription API endpoint has been updated to provide the id of the existing EventSub subscription when a 409 Conflict is returned." The repo previously ignored 409 and treated the body as a fresh creation.

> The Create EventSub Subscription API endpoint has been updated to provide the id of the existing EventSub subscription when a 409 Conflict is returned.

Source: https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/change-log/

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| conflict | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- conflict, added by the agent: `python tests/test_conflict.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `twitch__search_docs`: pass
- `twitch__fetch_changelog`: pass

Test of this change: `conflict`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Exact location of the id in the 409 body is not in the changelog; the helper checks body.id, data[0].id and data.id. The mocked test assumes a top-level id.
- No openapi validator was run.
- Dependency install failed on unrelated pinned packages, so the app was not imported; the test extracts the functions via ast.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- create_subscription's returned dict gains an existing_id key on 409 responses, and one extra line is printed. Nothing else changes.

review.summary: The API change is additive. Before, a 409 on Create EventSub Subscription simply returned an error body. The old code in src/app.py did not depend on that body: hello_chat ignores create_subscription's return value, and it only creates subscriptions missing from get_subscriptions(). ## channel.chat.message EventSub adds gif fragment type; IRC PRIVMSG gets gif tag (parsers may need handling) [Verified]

### Change

The bot has no EventSub chat handler. Its only chat parser is the IRC PRIVMSG regex in src/bot.py. That regex matches tags by name, so an extra `gif` tag is already tolerated. I moved the regex into a module-level PAT_MESSAGE constant, with no change to the pattern, so a test can load it. I added tests/test_gif_tag.py, which checks that PRIVMSG lines carrying a gif tag still parse.

Files touched:
- `src/bot.py`
- `tests/test_gif_tag.py`

### Why

Twitch IRC PRIVMSG now carries a new gif tag. The parser had to be confirmed to tolerate it. It does, so the change is a refactor plus a regression test.

> The channel.chat.message EventSub subscription type has been updated to include the new gif fragment type.

Source: https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/change-log/

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gif-tag | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- gif-tag, added by the agent: `python tests/test_gif_tag.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `gif-tag`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The real gif tag format is unknown; I only tested made-up values, including ones containing '/', '=' and ':'.
- The test fails on the original code only because PAT_MESSAGE did not exist there. It does not show a parse failure.
- No Twitch provider validator was run.
- Gif content in message text is stored and printed as-is.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- None. The regex is unchanged and is now a module-level constant.

The pattern is byte-for-byte the same; only the `fr` prefix became `r`, and with no braces in the pattern that changes nothing.
